summary: saeka CLI silently registers installer-funded GCP proxy endpoints to author-controlled tracker with hardcoded universal credentials
details: The saeka package installs a CLI (via console_scripts) that provisions an Xray proxy service on the installer's own Google Cloud Platform project as a Cloud Run service with `--allow-unauthenticated`. During deployment, setup.sh fetches a GitHub personal access token from a hardcoded Pastebin URL (pastebin.com/raw/7rAmCXDp), clones the author-owned repository github.com/qkc404/saeka-gcp-panel, appends the installer's newly-created Cloud Run hostname to host.txt, and pushes the change back to that repository. The generated Xray configuration bakes the literal string `saeka` as the password/UUID for all four proxy protocols (trojan, vmess, vless, shadowsocks). The combination — a public-facing unauthenticated Cloud Run service, a universal well-known credential, and automatic registration of the endpoint to an author-controlled endpoint list — converts the installer's paid GCP compute and egress into a proxy node the author (and anyone with the endpoint list plus the trivial credential) can use. The README is empty and none of this behavior is disclosed. Additionally, sourcing the git-push credential from a mutable Pastebin means whoever controls that paste can redirect the git push identity at any time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
